scope: Proposition 8.1 (Obstruction to multiplicative rectangles) of the manuscript “A power saving for planar unit distances” (preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-unit-distances-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 167 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 72bfa9153772b212), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is no sequence with the following properties. At index n, let tn → ∞, let Jn → ∞, and let Pn ⊂ R2 be a finite set of algebraic points with |Pn| ≤ t 1+o(1) n . Let Gn ⊂ Pn × Pn be a bipartite graph, using two copies of Pn, with at least t 2−o(1) n edges. To each edge (p, r) assign a nonzero algebraic number λpr. Suppose that, for an absolute c > 0, (zp − zr)(wp − wr) = 2 − λpr − λ−1 pr , (8.1) h(λpr) ≥ cJn, (8.2) h λprλp′r′ λpr′ λp′r ! = o(Jn) (8.3) uniformly over edges and complete rectangles, respectively. Finally, suppose that no edge has both endpoints on a unit circle containing at least t 9/10 n points of Pn. Here h is the absolute height from Theorem 4.2.
